_about: Common diagnoses seen in Indian prescriptions and discharge summaries, with ICD-10 (WHO/ICD-10-CM) and SNOMED CT codes, the aliases and abbreviations doctors write, the matching DOC profile condition (for care-gap rules), and a plain-language explanation. Explanations are general education, not advice.

items.name: Type 2 diabetes
items.simple: The body does not use sugar (glucose) properly, so blood sugar stays high. Diet, activity and medicines help keep it controlled.

items.name: Type 1 diabetes
items.simple: The body makes little or no insulin, so insulin injections are needed to control blood sugar.

items.name: Prediabetes
items.simple: Blood sugar is higher than normal but not yet diabetes. Lifestyle changes can often bring it back to normal.

items.name: Diabetic neuropathy
items.simple: Nerve damage from long-term high sugar. It can cause tingling, burning or numbness, usually in the feet.

items.name: High blood pressure (hypertension)
items.simple: Blood pushes too hard against artery walls. Over years this can strain the heart, kidneys and brain, so it is kept under control.

items.name: Hypothyroidism
items.simple: The thyroid gland makes too little hormone, which can cause tiredness, weight gain and feeling cold.

items.name: Hyperthyroidism
items.simple: The thyroid gland makes too much hormone, which can cause a fast heartbeat, weight loss and anxiety.

items.name: High cholesterol / blood fats (dyslipidaemia)
items.simple: Cholesterol or other blood fats are not at healthy levels, which raises the risk of heart attack and stroke over time.

items.name: Obesity
items.simple: Body weight is high for height. It raises the risk of diabetes, BP and joint problems.

items.name: Chronic kidney disease
items.simple: The kidneys have been working less well for months or years. Regular tests and BP/sugar control help slow it down.

items.name: Acute kidney injury
items.simple: The kidneys suddenly stopped working well, often during an illness or dehydration. Many people recover, but follow-up tests are important.

items.name: Coronary artery disease
items.simple: The arteries that feed the heart are narrowed. It can cause chest pain and raises the risk of heart attack.

items.name: Heart attack (myocardial infarction)
items.simple: Part of the heart muscle did not get enough blood. Medicines and follow-up help protect the heart.

items.name: Heart failure
items.simple: The heart is not pumping as well as it should. It can cause breathlessness and swelling of the legs.

items.name: Atrial fibrillation
items.simple: An irregular heartbeat. It can raise the risk of stroke, so doctors often check whether blood thinners are needed.

items.name: Stroke
items.simple: Blood supply to part of the brain was blocked or a vessel bled. Rehabilitation and preventing another stroke are key.

items.name: Asthma
items.simple: The airways get swollen and narrow at times, causing wheeze and breathlessness. Inhalers help control it.

items.name: COPD
items.simple: Long-term lung damage (often from smoke) that makes breathing harder. Inhalers and avoiding smoke help.

items.name: Pneumonia
items.simple: An infection of the lungs. Complete the full course of treatment and return if breathing gets worse.

items.name: Urinary tract infection
items.simple: An infection in the urine passages or bladder. Finish the full course of medicine and drink enough water unless told otherwise.

items.name: Dengue fever
items.simple: A viral fever spread by mosquitoes. Platelet counts are watched closely; warning signs need urgent care.

items.name: Typhoid fever
items.simple: A bacterial infection from contaminated food or water. Complete the full antibiotic course.

items.name: Malaria
items.simple: An infection spread by mosquitoes that causes fever with chills. It needs complete treatment.

items.name: COVID-19
items.simple: A viral infection that mainly affects the lungs. Watch oxygen levels and breathing during recovery.

items.name: Tuberculosis
items.simple: A bacterial infection, usually of the lungs. It is curable when the full course (often 6 months) is completed.

items.name: Anaemia
items.simple: Haemoglobin is low, so the blood carries less oxygen. It can cause tiredness and breathlessness.

items.name: Iron deficiency anaemia
items.simple: Anaemia caused by low iron. Iron-rich food and treatment usually fix it; the cause is also checked.

items.name: Fatty liver
items.simple: Extra fat is stored in the liver. Weight loss, exercise and sugar control can reverse it.

items.name: Liver cirrhosis
items.simple: Long-term scarring of the liver. Regular follow-up helps catch problems early.

items.name: Gastritis / acidity
items.simple: The stomach lining is irritated, causing burning pain or acidity.

items.name: Acid reflux (GERD)
items.simple: Stomach acid comes up into the food pipe, causing heartburn.

items.name: Gastroenteritis (loose motions)
items.simple: An infection of the stomach and gut causing vomiting or loose motions. Fluids (ORS) are the most important treatment.

items.name: Appendicitis
items.simple: The appendix became inflamed; it is usually treated with surgery or antibiotics.

items.name: PCOS
items.simple: A hormone condition that can cause irregular periods and weight gain. Lifestyle changes help a lot.

items.name: Osteoarthritis
items.simple: Wear of the joint cartilage, often in the knees, causing pain and stiffness.

items.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
items.simple: The immune system attacks the joints, causing pain and swelling. Regular specialist follow-up is important.

items.name: Gout
items.simple: Uric acid crystals in a joint cause sudden painful swelling, often in the big toe.

items.name: Depression
items.simple: A health condition that causes long-lasting low mood. It is treatable; talking to a doctor helps.

items.name: Migraine
items.simple: Repeated headaches, often one-sided with sensitivity to light. Knowing triggers helps.

items.name: Epilepsy / seizure disorder
items.simple: A tendency to have fits (seizures). Taking medicines regularly is very important.

items.name: Cellulitis (skin infection)
items.simple: A bacterial skin infection causing red, warm, painful skin. Spreading redness or fever needs a doctor.

items.name: Cataract
items.simple: The lens of the eye becomes cloudy, making vision blurry. It is treated with a simple operation.
